NAME: NetLiquidKnowledgeValue
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that are cheap on pre-R&D earnings yield and have net liquidity relative to their knowledge-adjusted asset base should outperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Prior evidence favored liquidity-conditioned intangible value, but gross cash alone may overstate financial flexibility when debt claims are large. This signal tests whether cheap intangible-intensive firms are most mispriced when they can sustain R&D without debt-overhang pressure or external financing dependence.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: SmoothedRDEnabledCostEfficiency
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(TREND(RATIO(cogs, revt), 3)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap pre-R&D earnings firms should outperform when cost intensity is persistently improving, indicating that intangible investment is translating into operating efficiency.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: A one-period gross-margin improvement can be noisy, so a short trend in COGS-to-revenue better captures sustained cost efficiency. The interaction requires both valuation support and evidence that R&D-adjusted earnings are backed by improving product economics rather than a mechanical R&D addback.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: EarningsPayoffOnPriorKnowledge
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 1), ADD(at, LAG(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), 1))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that are cheap on current pre-R&D earnings should outperform when prior accumulated knowledge investment is beginning to produce adjusted earnings improvement.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This shifts the payoff test from sales growth to bottom-line pre-R&D earnings improvement, which is closer to value realization. Scaling by assets plus lagged R&D capital links the improvement to the asset base that should have generated it, rather than rewarding growth disconnected from prior intangible investment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: LiquidPayoutKnowledgeYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(dvc, 0), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(che, ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high combined dividend-plus-R&D yield should outperform when they also hold enough liquidity to sustain both shareholder payout and knowledge investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Dividend-plus-R&D yield treats cash distributions and expensed knowledge investment as two investor-relevant uses of internal resources. The liquidity conditioner seeks firms where that yield is not merely a distress artifact, but is supported by a balance sheet capable of funding ongoing intangible investment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: StableAdjustedKnowledgeReturnValue
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(VOL(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 5)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap pre-R&D earnings yield should be more reliable when the firm’s R&D-adjusted return on assets is stable through time.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Adding back R&D can make speculative firms look cheap if adjusted profitability is erratic. Low volatility in adjusted return on a knowledge-inclusive asset base identifies firms where intangible investment appears to support durable earning power rather than one-off accounting noise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: RecognizedIntangibleSalesCoverValue
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(sale, ADD(sale, COALESCE(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: High earnings-yield firms should outperform more when reported intangible assets are well covered by sales, suggesting acquired or recognized intangibles are productive rather than overcapitalized.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This avoids treating intangibles as an extra claim added to market value and instead measures whether recognized intangible balances are supported by revenue scale. The signal favors cheap firms where accounting intangibles do not represent an unproductive balance-sheet burden. 
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE NetLiquidKnowledgeValue---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Substituting net cash for gross cash in the archive's strongest signal (LiquidKnowledgeValue, ls_talpha 4.695) is an economically defensible test of debt overhang versus raw liquidity, but it is a single-term swap on an already-tested construction and much of its variation will simply reload on the well-known low-leverage/cash-holdings tilt, so the incremental information content is modest.

---CRITIQUE SmoothedRDEnabledCostEfficiency---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a cosmetic smoothing variant of RDEnabledCostEfficiencyValue (DELTA→TREND on the identical COGS/revenue conditioner with an identical value leg), exactly the kind of parameter tweak the objective warns against rather than a substantively different mechanism.

---CRITIQUE EarningsPayoffOnPriorKnowledge---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Beyond being a one-variable respecification of PriorKnowledgeCashPayoffValue (oancf→ib+xrd), the change induces mechanical overlap because the same ib+xrd quantity now drives both legs — firms with rising pre-R&D earnings mechanically tend toward higher pre-R&D earnings yield — so the "interaction" partly double-counts a single earnings-growth effect already spanned by the profitability-change literature.

---CRITIQUE LiquidPayoutKnowledgeYield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a direct recombination of two already-evaluated archive components (PayoutSupportedKnowledgeYield's dividend-plus-R&D yield leg and LiquidKnowledgeValue's che/knowledge-asset leg) with no new construct, and cash-rich high-payout firms are close to a plain quality/payout screen already spanned by prior tests.

---CRITIQUE StableAdjustedKnowledgeReturnValue---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Conditioning R&D-adjusted earnings yield on the stability of R&D-adjusted ROA is a coherent and internally consistent test that differs meaningfully from StableRDProgramValue (which stabilized R&D intensity, not profitability), though it sits close to the well-documented earnings-volatility/quality-value interaction and the 5-year VOL requirement will thin coverage.

---CRITIQUE RecognizedIntangibleSalesCoverValue---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The hypothesis claims to identify "productive" recognized intangibles, but sale/(sale+intan) is just a monotone transform of low intangible intensity that assigns the maximum score of 1.0 to the large mass of firms with zero or missing intan, producing severe rank ties and reducing the signal to a value × no-goodwill tilt already covered by GoodwillCleanBookValue and InternalKnowledgeBookValueQuality.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: DurableKnowledgeDemandValue
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(VOL(RATIO(revt, ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 5)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that are cheap on pre-R&D earnings yield should outperform when revenue productivity on a knowledge-adjusted asset base is stable.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This replaces the cosmetic COGS/revenue smoothing change with a demand-durability mechanism. The signal asks whether R&D-adjusted cheapness is supported by persistent revenue generation from the asset base, rather than by a one-period margin fluctuation or a mechanical R&D addback.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: KnowledgeDeleveragingValue
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), ADD(at, LAG(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), 1))), 1)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Cheap pre-R&D earnings firms should outperform when leverage is falling relative to the asset base that includes prior accumulated knowledge investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This avoids double-counting the same pre-R&D earnings variable in both legs. The mechanism is financial payoff from intangible investment: if prior knowledge capital is becoming self-sustaining, the firm should need less debt support, making the valuation discount more credible.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: BalancedDividendInnovationYield
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(COALESCE(dvc, 0), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(ABS(ib), ADD(COALESCE(dvc, 0), COALESCE(xrd, 0)))), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that are cheap because they simultaneously return cash to shareholders and invest meaningfully in R&D should outperform when those uses of funds are supported by earnings.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: This is not a recombination of payout yield and liquidity; it uses the bottleneck between dividends and R&D to identify firms doing both, rather than firms with only one large component. The support leg helps avoid distressed or speculative firms where dividend-plus-R&D intensity is high only because earnings are weak.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: ProductiveRecognizedIntangibleValue
EXPRESSION: ADD(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(ib, MUL(prcc_f, csho)), 1)), MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(COALESCE(intan, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1), 1)))))
HYPOTHESIS: High earnings-yield firms should outperform more when they have meaningful recognized intangible assets and improving gross-profit productivity.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This avoids assigning the highest score to firms with zero or missing recognized intangibles; firms without recognized intangibles receive only the baseline earnings-yield component. The amplifier is strongest when recognized intangible intensity is economically material and gross profit relative to assets is improving, indicating that recorded intangible assets are productive rather than merely absent.
